preserved_objections.basis: The proposed mechanism of reducing compressive loading on pouch cells through a mechanical support system does not address the root cause of lithium plating on the graphite anode during fast charging, which is a result of the high charge rate and the inherent properties of lithium-ion batteries. This is evident from the study [doi:10.54337/aau681516574], which identifies the high charge rate as a primary factor contributing to lithium plating and capacity fade.

The proposed boundary condition of 350 kW charge rate and 15-minute depot turnaround is not realistic for most electric bus depots, where the charge rate is typically limited to 150-200 kW. This is evident from the study [doi:10.2139/ssrn.4766704], which suggests that high charge rates above 200 kW can lead to increased lithium plating and capacity fade.

The study [doi:10.1109/acpee56931.2023.10135597] on fast charging methods of lithium titanate batteries contradicts the proposed solution, as it suggests that lithium titanate batteries are more resistant to lithium plating and capacity fade during fast charging. This contradicts the proposed solution, which aims to mitigate these effects in lithium-titanate-free batteries.

The proposed solution does not provide any evidence that it can outperform the baseline, which is the current implementation of electric-bus depot lithium-titanate-free fast-charging battery packs. The study [doi:10.5281/zenodo.17872087] provides a comprehensive review of various battery chemistries, but it does not provide any evidence that the proposed solution can outperform the baseline.
